## claude.ai Datadog
This is an MCP server for Datadog (a software observability platform). Consult Datadog docs if you're unsure about how something works in the platform. Docs for this MCP server can be found at https://docs.datadoghq.com/bits_ai/mcp_server/setup/ This server ships skill guides containing domain-specific guidance, workflows, and best practices that are not visible in tool names or schemas. Before invoking other tools, always perform skill discovery by running both paths in parallel: a direct load with `load_datadog_skill` using a general domain name (e.g. skill_name='datadog/traces'), and a call to `list_datadog_skills` with a fuzzy `query` based on topic keywords — load any clearly matching result from the listing along with the related skills it points to. The exception is a follow-up call in a domain whose skill you have already loaded or confirmed absent this session. If nothing clearly fits, do not load a skill — proceed with the tool descriptions. When the user asks to visualize, chart, or graph data — or when loading a data domain skill (e.g. datadog/traces, datadog/logs, datadog/metrics) — also load datadog/visualizations. Investigation results often benefit from charts.

## claude.ai entire-prod-us
Entire MCP — an investigation surface over Entire's engineering data: repos and their analytics, git history (commits, files, trees, refs, diffs), the AI checkpoints and sessions behind the code (with transcripts and token accounting), trails (PR-like change proposals), and code search. Reads are curated `*_entire` tools; a small write/ops group covers trail/review/runner/dispatch mutations.

Workflow: when you only have a repo name, path, or URL, call resolve_entire_repo first, then pass the repo it returns to repo-scoped tools. Prefer the aggregation tools (get_entire_repo_overview, get_entire_my_activity) over hand-rolling stats from raw listings.

Querying conventions (shared by every tool):
- Addressing: name a repo by a prefixed path (gh/<owner>/<repo>, et/<project>/<repo>, git/<owner>/<repo>) or a repo ULID. Repo ULIDs are REGION-SCOPED — the same repo has a different ULID per region, so never carry a ULID across regions or sessions; if a tool rejects one, re-resolve with resolve_entire_repo.
- Pagination: every list takes an opaque cursor and returns next_cursor when more remains — exhaust the pages before concluding "that's all".
- Time: since/until are ISO 8601 / RFC3339 bounds; where offered, timeframe is a relative window (last-month, last-3-months, last-6-months).
- Size: reads that can be large (files, diffs, transcripts) honor max_tokens and return next_cursor to continue — raise max_tokens or page rather than assuming truncation is the whole story.

Pitfalls:
- sessions[].tokenUsage on a checkpoint is a PER-CHECKPOINT delta, not a session total — sum across a session's checkpoints, or use get_entire_session for the authoritative total.
- list_entire_checkpoints silently truncates older history; for a branch's COMPLETE checkpoint membership, paginate list_entire_commits and collect the per-commit checkpoint IDs.

Skills: before deep work in a domain, load the matching skill (list_entire_skills / load_entire_skill) — entire/checkpoints-and-sessions and entire/token-analysis before token accounting, … [truncated]

## claude.ai incident.io
The incident.io MCP server lets you query and manage incidents, alerts, escalations, schedules, follow-ups, catalog data, and telemetry.

If another connected MCP server exposes an incident_pin tool (alongside incident_list, incident_show, etc.), that is the incident.io desktop server — prefer it for every incident.io action. It is a superset of this one: it proxies these same tools and adds local-only capabilities (the user's pinned incident, locally-cached investigations, opening links). Don't split a task across both servers — in particular, an ask / ask_incident / ask_telemetry session_id from this server is not valid on the desktop server, so keep each conversation on whichever server it started on.

Before you start:
- Read config://organisation to discover severity IDs, custom field IDs, role IDs, and other values you'll need for filtering and grouping.
- Read playbook://analysis before doing any analytical or reporting work — it indexes all analysis playbooks and helps you pick the right one for the user's question. Then call analysis_start to download the playbook workspace.

Tool selection:
- analysis_start — call this BEFORE doing any analytical or reporting work (e.g. "analyse my incidents", "prepare for the review", "how are we doing?"). It downloads playbooks with step-by-step methodology, org config, and a branded HTML report template. Follow the playbook stages rather than ad-hoc querying — it produces much better analysis.
- stats tools (incident_stats, alert_stats, escalation_stats, follow_up_stats) — for counts, trends, and workload breakdowns across many records. Start here for analytical questions.
- list tools (incident_list, alert_list, etc.) — to browse or search individual records. Use the include parameter on incident_list to enrich results with roles or custom fields without calling incident_show for each one.
- show tools (incident_show, alert_show, etc.) — for full detail on a specific record. For investigation or root cause analysis, always request include: ["investigation", "postmor… [truncated]

Use only when the user explicitly mentions Herdr or asks to use Herdr to inspect or control panes, tabs, workspaces, terminals, commands, or communication with another agent. Use for any Cloudflare development task. Biases towards retrieval from Cloudflare docs over pre-trained knowledge.

Use when building email sending (Workers binding or REST API), email routing, Agents SDK email handling, or integrating email into any app — Workers, Node.js, Python, Go, etc. Also use for email deliverability, SPF/DKIM/DMARC, wrangler email setup, MCP email tools, or when a coding agent needs to send emails. Use when users ask to audit, analyze, validate, review, or security-check a GitOps repo.

- design: Create a design canvas - a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces - posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.

{"id":"ENT-2054","title":"Interrupted batched bootstrap can never resume: the resume ref disqualifies the bootstrap route","description":"## Summary

git-sync's batched bootstrap writes a resume marker (`refs/gitsync/bootstrap/heads/<branch>`) so an interrupted run can pick up where it left off. It also has real logic to do that: `BootstrapResumeIndex`, chain-position recovery, and the "resuming from stale temp ref" re-plan at `bootstrap.go:352`.

**That logic is unreachable from mirror-worker.** The marker it resumes from is exactly what stops the bootstrap strategy from being selected on the next pass. Once a batched bootstrap is interrupted for any reason, the repo is routed to `replicate` forever — and `replicate` has no batching.

<issue id="5b7a6b15-b273-4116-a4a4-0c2147883e72" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1948/mirror-sync-permanently-fails-when-catch-up-pack-exceeds-10-gib">ENT-1948</issue> is one instance of this (the interruption there was the 10 GiB receive-pack cap). This ticket is the reason that instance never heals, and it generalises past that cap.

## The chain

All read in code, not inferred:

1. mirror-worker syncs with `AllRefs: true` + `Prune: true` and no `Mappings` — `mirror-pipeline/cmd/worker/syncer.go:652` (`refScopeFor`), `:707` (`syncPolicyFor`).
2. `excludeRefPrefixes` (`cmd/worker/syncer.go:80-105`) does **not** contain `refs/gitsync/`. It carves out other tooling-owned namespaces — `refs/tlog/`, `refs/meta/entire/`, `refs/internal/` — but this one was missed.
3. `syncer.replicateCanBootstrap` (`git-sync/internal/syncer/syncer.go:1157`) passes its desired-refs loop (the target genuinely has no `refs/heads/main`), but because `Prune` is set it then walks **every** target ref. `refs/gitsync/bootstrap/heads/main` is non-zero, not desired, and not excluded; `planner.RefKindFromName` returns `RefKindOther` (`planner/types.go:142` — `IsBranch()` requires a `refs/heads/` prefix), which matches the `AllRefs && RefKindOther && no Mappings` case → **returns false**.
4. `allAbsent == false` → `bootstrapWithInputs` is skipped → `BuildReplicationPlans` → `executeReplicate` → a single unbatched pack.
5. When that push fails, the temp ref is never cleaned up either: `replicate.Execute` pushes updates before deletes and returns on update failure (`internal/strategy/replicate/replicate.go:62-79`), so the prune that would have removed the marker never runs.

Every subsequent sync makes the identical decision. The artifact of the one attempt that *was* using the right strategy is what locks that strategy out.

## Scope

Any repo whose batched bootstrap is interrupted — OOM, pod eviction, deploy, context cancel, deadline, or a receive-pack rejection. The interruption cause is incidental; the lock is the same. Confirmed instance: `gh/nicschick/vc3r` (`01KXK4WZWXD1PEP16K9V6CMFHA`, eu-central-1), stranded since 2026-07-15, ~5 MB / 19 loose objects / 0 packfiles behind a bootstrap temp ref with no `refs/heads/main`.

`refs/gitsync/` is written **only** by git-sync — constructed in one place, `planner.BootstrapTempRef` (`internal/planner/types.go:227`) — and git-sync deletes it itself on success (`bootstrap.go:654`) or when stale (`:378`). entiredb has no awareness of the namespace at all (no references in `refpolicy`, `server`, or `mirror`), so it is an ordinary ref there: listable, pushable, prunable. A leftover `refs/gitsync/*` ref therefore means one thing only — a bootstrap that did not finish — and nothing outside git-sync reads it.

### Second instance: `gh/nicschick/rci`

`01KXK4WZS7M270NSABM94DRF01`, same GitHub App install (146778232), created within the same minute as `vc3r` on 2026-07-15. Identical ref shape — `HEAD` → `refs/heads/main` (absent) plus `refs/gitsync/bootstrap/heads/main` → `93b964ac`, nothing else.

It matters because **its interruption was demonstrably not the 10 GiB cap**: 4 packfiles totalling 354 MB were written between 15:09:36Z and 15:50:59Z on 2026-07-15, so the fetch landed, and it has **zero **`@target_ulid` telemetry in the last 30 days — no sync jobs at all, failing or otherwise. Most likely a dormant upstream (no pushes → no jobs). That makes it a *latent* instance rather than an actively-burning one: the moment a push arrives it takes exactly the path described above.

This is the concrete evidence for the "interruption cause is incidental" claim in Scope — two repos, same lock, different interruptions.

## Proposed fixes

**Primary — see the marker and resume from it.** Route on the marker's *presence*: a `refs/gitsync/bootstrap/*` ref means a bootstrap started and did not finish, which is strictly more information than "the target has no managed refs". Check it ahead of the emptiness heuristic and send the repo to the bootstrap strategy, which then resumes from that exact ref.

Why this shape rather than hiding the ref:

* **It is a positive signal.** The namespace has exactly one writer and exactly one meaning. Using it directly is honest; the alternative below makes the system conclude "this repo is empty", which is false — it is half-bootstrapped. Right routing for the wrong reason.
* **It does not depend on the marker being the only stray ref.** The exclusion works on `vc3r` only because nothing else sits in the target ref map. One additional leftover ref — an aborted sync, a branch deleted upstream mid-bootstrap, a manual push — and the repo wedges again for the same underlying reason.
* The resume machinery is already written and currently unreachable. `BootstrapResumeIndex`, the chain-position re-plan (`bootstrap.go:352`), stale-marker deletion (`:378`), and the per-branch subsume when a branch is already complete (`:249`). This is the wiring that turns all of it on rather than new logic.

Edge cases the existing code already covers: a stale marker (pointing at a commit no longer in the source chain) is re-planned from its chain position or deleted; a marker left behind on an otherwise-complete repo degrades to a no-op via the per-branch subsume check.

**Stopgap (one line, unblocks today):** add `refs/gitsync/` to `excludeRefPrefixes` in `cmd/worker/syncer.go:80`, alongside the existing `refs/tlog/` and `refs/meta/entire/` entries. This makes the marker invisible to `replicateCanBootstrap`, so the check returns "bootstrappable" and the repo takes the bootstrap path. Useful to unblock `vc3r` now, but it is not the end state — see the second bullet above for why it is fragile.

**Also worth doing:** run deletes before updates in `replicate.Execute` (`internal/strategy/replicate/replicate.go:62-79`), so a prune still lands when the pack push fails. Independent of the above, and closes the "the failure prevents its own cleanup" half of the trap.

**Considered and set aside:** routing on entiredb's `MirrorInitialSyncDone` flag. It tells you the import is unfinished but not *where to pick up*, and it needs plumbing from entiredb into the job payload. The marker answers both questions and is already local to git-sync.

## Implementation notes

For whoever picks this up — routing to bootstrap is necessary but not automatically sufficient:

* **Auto-batching is gated on source capability. **`SupportsBootstrapBatch()` (`internal/gitproto/fetch.go:33`) requires `Protocol == "v2"` **and **`V2Caps.FetchSupports("filter")`. True for GitHub, so `vc3r` is fine — but a non-v2 source would reach bootstrap and still fail unbatched. Any fix that only changes routing inherits this gate.
* **Setting** `TargetMaxPackBytes` **in the worker would *disable* the reactive path. **`autoTargetMaxPackBytes` returns early when `p.TargetMaxPack > 0` (`bootstrap.go:1386`). mirror-worker currently passes no pack options at all (`cmd/worker/syncer.go:399`), which is precisely why auto-detection is eligible. Counterintuitive — worth a comment at whichever site ends up owning it.
* **Batch sizing:** the auto path takes the min of `defaultTargetMaxPackBytes` (512 MiB), half the limit announced in the rejection, and `MaxPackBytes` when set.
* **Subdivision has a floor. **`subdivideCheckpoints` halves commit ranges until every gap is one commit, so a *single* commit whose delta exceeds the cap still fails. Not yet checked whether `vc3r`'s >10 GiB spans multiple commits — worth confirming before assuming this fix converges that specific repo.
* **The target must permit non-fast-forward updates on** `refs/gitsync/` (`git-sync/docs/usage.md:97`, `unstable/client.go:52`). Fine today since entiredb has no policy on the namespace, but it constrains any future reserved-ref work there.

## Verification status

The chain above is read from source and matches the error string observed in <issue id="5b7a6b15-b273-4116-a4a4-0c2147883e72" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1948/mirror-sync-permanently-fails-when-catch-up-pack-exceeds-10-gib">ENT-1948</issue> (`replicate relay failed: replicate execute: push target refs: ...`). The routing decision itself is **not** logged — mirror-worker records `operation: sync_repo` but not the sync result's `OperationMode` / `RelayReason`. A `git-sync` dry-run against that source/target prints `BootstrapSuggested` and `RelayReason` directly and would confirm it in one shot.

**Suggested follow-up regardless of fix:** log `OperationMode` and `RelayReason` from mirror-worker. 60	// prefix + "/" and so never reaches the bare anchor. Keep in lockstep with the
61	// reservedExact set in entiredb's refpolicy/refpolicy.go.
62	var reservedAncestorRefs = []string{
63		"refs/heads/entire",
64		"refs/heads/entire/unmirrored",
65		"refs/meta",
66		"refs/meta/entire",
67	}
68	
69	// excludeRefPrefixes are the source ref namespaces the worker never mirrors
70	// (and, being unmirrored, never prunes) on a GITHUB sync. Shared between the
71	// sync scope and the default-branch reconcile guard: a source HEAD under one
72	// of these prefixes can never land on the target, so the reconcile treats it
73	// as non-convergent rather than looping forever (see isNonMirrorableBranch —
74	// which deliberately keeps checking THIS list for both kinds, because
75	// entiredb's SetDefaultBranch rejects an unmirrored-namespace default
76	// unconditionally). The refs/heads/ entries here are the only ones a HEAD
77	// could point at; the rest are kept for a single source of truth with the
78	// sync scope. entiredb-kind syncs use excludeRefPrefixesFor, which drops
79	// exactly one entry.
80	var excludeRefPrefixes = []string{
81		"refs/pull/",
82		"refs/heads/trunk-merge/",
83		"refs/heads/gh-readonly-queue/",
84		"refs/tlog/",
85		"refs/remotes/",
86		"refs/internal/",
87		"refs/replace/",
88		"refs/bisect/",
89	
90		// Only Entire's own managed sub-namespace is reserved, NOT all of
91		// refs/meta/. entiredb reserves refs/meta/entire/* (refpolicy's
92		// ManagedMetaPrefix) and carves it out for the entire-api workload alone,
93		// which the worker is not — so the worker must still skip it. The rest of
94		// refs/meta/* is unreserved by design: standard git-meta clients push
95		// refs/meta/config and friends directly, and those mirror like any other
96		// ref. See entiredb refpolicy/refpolicy.go and its ADR
97		// docs/adrs/20260603-reserved-refs.md.
98		"refs/meta/entire/",
99	
100		"refs/namespaces/",
101		"refs/stash", // covers the exact refs/stash ref and refs/stash/*
102	
103		// refs/heads/entire/unmirrored/* are Entire-only branches (see
104		// unmirroredRefPrefix). Excluded so Prune never deletes one for being
105		// absent on GitHub; the outbound push-through skip that keeps them off
106		// GitHub lives in entiredb.
107		unmirroredRefPrefix,
108	}
109	
110	// excludeRefPrefixesFor returns the sync-scope exclusions for a source kind.
111	// An entiredb-kind sync (native mirroring) drops exactly the unmirrored-
112	// namespace exclusion and nothing else (plan decision 3, ADR
113	// 20260720-native-mirroring): that exclusion exists to keep Entire-only
114	// branches out of a GitHub round-trip, and when the source IS entiredb the
115	// namespace replicates like any branch — a native mirror is a full read-only
116	// copy. Everything else stays excluded for the same reasons as GitHub:
117	// refs/tlog/* is per-placement entiredb-owned state receive-pack rejects,
118	// and the reserved namespaces would 403 the push.
119	func excludeRefPrefixesFor(kind gitjobs.SourceKind) []string {
120		if kind != gitjobs.SourceKindEntireDB {
121			return excludeRefPrefixes
122		}
123		out := make([]string, 0, len(excludeRefPrefixes)-1)
124		for _, p := range excludeRefPrefixes {
125			if p != unmirroredRefPrefix {
126				out = append(out, p)
127			}
128		}
129		return out
130	}

1	// Package bootstrap implements the bootstrap relay strategy for git-sync.
2	// This handles initial seeding of an empty target, both one-shot and batched.
3	package bootstrap
4	
5	import (
6		"bytes"
7		"context"
8		"encoding/json"
9		"errors"
10		"fmt"
11		"io"
12		"log/slog"
13		"net/http"
14		"regexp"
15		"strconv"
16		"strings"
17	
18		git "github.com/go-git/go-git/v6"
19		"github.com/go-git/go-git/v6/plumbing"
20	
21		"entire.io/entire/git-sync/internal/convert"
22		"entire.io/entire/git-sync/internal/gitproto"
23		"entire.io/entire/git-sync/internal/planner"
24		"entire.io/entire/git-sync/internal/useragent"
25	)
26	
27	const (
28		defaultTargetMaxPackBytes  = 512 * 1024 * 1024
29		githubLargeRepoThresholdKB = 1536 * 1024
30	)
31	
32	var bodyLimitPattern = regexp.MustCompile(`body exceeded size limit ([0-9]+)`)
33	
34	// GitHubRepoAPIBaseURL is the base for GitHub API calls (replaceable in tests).
35	var GitHubRepoAPIBaseURL = "https://api.github.com"
36	
37	// Params holds the inputs for a bootstrap execution.
38	type Params struct {
39		SourceConn    gitproto.Conn
40		SourceService interface {
41			FetchPack(ctx context.Context, conn gitproto.Conn, desired map[plumbing.ReferenceName]gitproto.DesiredRef, haves map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash) (io.ReadCloser, error)
42			FetchCommitParents(ctx context.Context, conn gitproto.Conn, ref gitproto.DesiredRef, haves []plumbing.Hash) (map[plumbing.Hash][]plumbing.Hash, error)
43			SupportsBootstrapBatch() bool
44		}
45		TargetPusher interface {
46			PushPack(ctx context.Context, cmds []gitproto.PushCommand, pack io.ReadCloser) error
47			PushCommands(ctx context.Context, cmds []gitproto.PushCommand) error
48		}
49		DesiredRefs map[plumbing.ReferenceName]planner.DesiredRef
50		TargetRefs  map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash
51		// SourceHeadTarget is the source ref that HEAD points to, when advertised.
52		// Empty if unknown. When set, batched bootstrap plans this branch first and
53		// uses its commit-graph reachability as a cutoff for subsequent branches.
54		SourceHeadTarget plumbing.ReferenceName
55		MaxPackBytes     int64
56		TargetMaxPack    int64
57		Verbose          bool
58		Logger           *slog.Logger
59		// Strategy selects the chain ordering for batched bootstrap. Empty
60		// or "first-parent" walks the first-parent backbone (default,
61		// matches historical behaviour). "topo" includes every reachable
62		// commit in topological order so sub-pack boundaries can land
63		// inside merge-pulled side branches — useful for repos like
64		// "checkpoint" branches where each first-parent step drags in a
65		// large second-parent ancestry that would otherwise have to be
66		// pushed in one indivisible pack.
67		//
68		// Server requirement under "topo": successive checkpoints aren't
69		// always in an ancestor-descendant relationship (topological
70		// order can interleave parallel branches), so the internal
71		// refs/gitsync/bootstrap/heads/<branch> temp ref may receive
72		// non-fast-forward updates between checkpoints. The temp ref is
73		// purely internal scaffolding — user-visible refs (refs/heads,
74		// refs/tags) only receive a single fast-forward update at
75		// cutover — but targets that enforce receive.denyNonFastforwards
76		// across all refs (not just refs/heads) will reject these
77		// updates and fail the bootstrap. Major hosts (GitHub, GitLab,
78		// Bitbucket, Cloudflare) do not enable this by default; the
79		// constraint only matters on hardened/locked-down deployments.
80		Strategy string
81		// OnPhase, when non-nil, is called with a short human-readable label
82		// describing the current bootstrap activity (e.g. "pack 3/8") so a
83		// live progress renderer can surface what is currently in flight.
84		// Called from the goroutine driving Execute; implementations must not
85		// block.
86		OnPhase func(string)
87		// OnNotice, when non-nil, receives one-time human-readable messages
88		// about discrete events worth surfacing alongside progress (pack
89		// subdivision, switching to batched mode). Implementations should
90		// treat each call as one log line.
91		OnNotice func(string)
92	}
93	
94	func (p Params) notice(msg string) {
95		if p.OnNotice != nil {
96			p.OnNotice(msg)
97		}
98	}
99	
100	// Result holds the outcome of the bootstrap strategy. Pushed is the count
101	// of attempted ref creates; under BestEffort, callers that want a count
102	// excluding rejected refs need to consult Pusher.OnRejection or apply the
103	// same downgrade pass the syncer wrapper does.
104	type Result struct {
105		Plans             []planner.BranchPlan
106		Pushed            int
107		Relay             bool
108		RelayMode         string
109		RelayReason       string
110		Batching          bool
111		BatchCount        int
112		PlannedBatchCount int
113		TempRefs          []string
114	}

116	type plannedBatch struct {
117		planner.BootstrapBatch
118	
119		chain []plumbing.Hash // full first-parent chain (root→tip) for subdividing on push failure
120		// subsumed is true when the branch tip is already reachable from the
121		// trunk (planned first), so every object is already on the target after
122		// trunk's batches. Execution skips the commit-graph fetch, the pack
123		// fetch, the temp ref, and the pack push — emitting only a single ref
124		// create command.
125		subsumed bool
126	}

128	// Execute runs the bootstrap strategy (one-shot or batched).
129	func Execute(ctx context.Context, p Params, relayReason string) (Result, error) {

148		}

150		result := Result{
151			Plans: plans, Relay: true, RelayMode: "bootstrap", RelayReason: relayReason,
152		}
153	
154		if p.TargetMaxPack > 0 {
155			return executeBatched(ctx, p, plans, result)
156		}
157	
158		// One-shot bootstrap
159		p.log("bootstrap fetching refs from source", "ref_count", len(plans))
160		gpDesired := convert.DesiredRefs(p.DesiredRefs)
161		packReader, err := p.SourceService.FetchPack(ctx, p.SourceConn, gpDesired, nil)
162		if err != nil {
163			if errors.Is(err, git.NoErrAlreadyUpToDate) {
164				return result, nil
165			}

167		}
168		packReader = gitproto.LimitPackReader(packReader, p.MaxPackBytes)
169		packReader = gitproto.CloseOnce(packReader)

171		p.log("bootstrap pushing refs to target", "ref_count", len(plans))
172		if p.OnPhase != nil {

174		}
175		cmds := convert.PlansToPushCommands(hoistSourceHeadPlan(plans, p.SourceHeadTarget), false)
176		pushErr := p.TargetPusher.PushPack(ctx, cmds, packReader)
177		_ = packReader.Close()

179			autoBatch, ok := autoTargetMaxPackBytes(p, pushErr)
180			if !ok {
181				return result, fmt.Errorf("push target refs: %w", actionableTargetPushError(p, pushErr))
182			}
183			reason := "target rejected pack"
184			if isTargetPushDeadlineError(pushErr) {

186			}
187			p.log("bootstrap retrying with batched mode after batchable push failure",
188				"target_max_pack_bytes", autoBatch, "reason", reason)
189			p.notice(fmt.Sprintf("%s — switching to batched mode (limit %s)",

199	// hoistSourceHeadPlan moves the plan whose source ref matches the
200	// source's symref HEAD target to the front, so the resulting push
201	// commands send that ref first. Hosts that pick the default branch
202	// from the first push on a fresh repo (GitHub, GitLab) end up with the
203	// right default. Matching is on SourceRef rather than TargetRef so
204	// --map remappings push the correct (mapped) target ref first.
205	func hoistSourceHeadPlan(plans []planner.BranchPlan, sourceHEAD plumbing.ReferenceName) []planner.BranchPlan {
206		if sourceHEAD == "" {
207			return plans
208		}
209		out, _ := hoistFirstMatch(plans, func(p planner.BranchPlan) bool {
210			return p.SourceRef == sourceHEAD
211		})
212		return out
213	}
214	
215	// hoistFirstMatch moves the first element satisfying match to the front
216	// of xs. Returns the (possibly new) slice and the original index of the
217	// hoisted element (-1 when no match). When the match is already at
218	// position 0, returns the input slice unchanged.
219	func hoistFirstMatch[T any](xs []T, match func(T) bool) ([]T, int) {
220		for i, x := range xs {
221			if !match(x) {
222				continue
223			}
224			if i == 0 {
225				return xs, 0
226			}
227			out := make([]T, 0, len(xs))
228			out = append(out, x)
229			out = append(out, xs[:i]...)
230			out = append(out, xs[i+1:]...)
231			return out, i
232		}
233		return xs, -1
234	}

236	func adjustedBootstrapTargetRefs(
237		desiredRefs map[plumbing.ReferenceName]planner.DesiredRef,
238		targetRefs map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash,
239	) map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash {
240		if len(targetRefs) == 0 {
241			return targetRefs
242		}
243		adjusted := planner.CopyRefHashMap(targetRefs)
244		for targetRef, desired := range desiredRefs {
245			if desired.Kind != planner.RefKindBranch {
246				continue
247			}
248			tempRef := planner.BootstrapTempRef(targetRef)
249			if adjusted[targetRef] == desired.SourceHash && adjusted[tempRef] == desired.SourceHash {
250				adjusted[targetRef] = plumbing.ZeroHash
251			}
252		}
253		return adjusted
254	}

258	func executeBatched( //nolint:maintidx // complex batch logic is inherently branchy
259		ctx context.Context,
260		p Params,
261		plans []planner.BranchPlan,
262		result Result,
263	) (Result, error) {
264		if !p.SourceService.SupportsBootstrapBatch() {
265			return result, errors.New("bootstrap batching requires protocol v2 source fetch filter support")
266		}

268		// Tags and other-kind refs are create-only and ride a single tail phase
269		// after the checkpointed branch batches; they reuse branch-tip haves.
270		planRefs := make([]planner.DesiredRef, 0, len(plans))
271		tailPlans := make([]planner.BranchPlan, 0, len(plans))
272		for _, plan := range plans {
273			if plan.Kind == planner.RefKindTag || plan.Kind == planner.RefKindOther {
274				tailPlans = append(tailPlans, plan)
275				continue
276			}
277			if !plan.SourceRef.IsBranch() || !plan.TargetRef.IsBranch() {
278				return result, errors.New("bootstrap batching currently supports branch refs, tags, and other-kind create-only refs")
279			}
280			planRefs = append(planRefs, p.DesiredRefs[plan.TargetRef])
281		}
282		tailDesired := convert.DesiredRefsForPlans(p.DesiredRefs, tailPlans)
283	
284		var batches []plannedBatch
285		if len(planRefs) > 0 {
286			p.log("bootstrap batch planning checkpoints", "branch_ref_count", len(planRefs))
287			var err error
288			batches, err = planBatches(ctx, p, planRefs)
289			if err != nil {
290				return result, err
291			}
292		}
293	
294		// MaxPackBytes is the hard abort threshold for any single source fetch.
295		// TargetMaxPack controls checkpoint *placement* (how many batches) but
296		// should not cap individual fetches — the estimate may undercount, and
297		// the actual pack for a batch can legitimately exceed the planning
298		// heuristic. If the resulting pack is too large for the target's
299		// receive-pack, the push itself fails and resume handles retry.
300		fetchLimit := p.MaxPackBytes
301		// Track branch tips already pushed to the target so subsequent branches
302		// can advertise them as haves. Without this, the second branch in a
303		// multi-branch bootstrap re-sends all shared objects (e.g., linux's
304		// master and nocache-cleanup share ~99% of history).
305		completedRefs := planner.CopyRefHashMap(p.TargetRefs)
306	
307		// calibratedBytesPerObject tracks the per-object byte estimate
308		// updated from observed rejected pushes. Starts at the static
309		// default (which under-counts blob-heavy repos) and ratchets up as
310		// 413s reveal that the real bytes/object are much higher than 750.
311		// Used in checkPackSizeAndSubdivide so subsequent sub-pack fetches
312		// are pre-emptively split when the calibrated estimate exceeds
313		// p.TargetMaxPack — saving an entire ~limit-sized wasted upload.
314		calibratedBytesPerObject := int64(estimatedBytesPerObject)
315	
316		// selfImposedBudget tracks the byte ceiling we use for mid-stream
317		// abort. Initialised from the user-supplied target limit; ratchets
318		// down each time we observe a smaller server-side cutoff (parsed
319		// 413 limit or, more commonly with reverse proxies that don't
320		// announce the limit in the response, the bytes we managed to send
321		// before the connection was cut). Re-used across attempts so every
322		// failed push refines the budget.
323		selfImposedBudget := p.TargetMaxPack

325		for _, batch := range batches {
326			if batch.subsumed {
327				cmds := []gitproto.PushCommand{{
328					Name: batch.Plan.TargetRef,
329					Old:  plumbing.ZeroHash,
330					New:  batch.Plan.SourceHash,
331				}}
332				if err := p.TargetPusher.PushCommands(ctx, cmds); err != nil {
333					return result, fmt.Errorf("create subsumed branch ref for %s: %w", batch.Plan.TargetRef, err)
334				}
335				completedRefs[batch.Plan.TargetRef] = batch.Plan.SourceHash
336				result.BatchCount++
337				p.log("bootstrap batch subsumed branch finalized",
338					"branch", batch.Plan.TargetRef.String(),
339					"source_hash", planner.ShortHash(batch.Plan.SourceHash))
340				continue
341			}
342			result.PlannedBatchCount += len(batch.Checkpoints)
343			result.TempRefs = append(result.TempRefs, batch.TempRef.String())
344			p.log("bootstrap batch branch plan",
345				"branch", batch.Plan.TargetRef.String(),
346				"temp_ref", batch.TempRef.String(),
347				"planned_batches", len(batch.Checkpoints),
348				"resume_hash", planner.ShortHash(batch.ResumeHash))
349	
350			current := batch.ResumeHash
351			startIdx, err := planner.BootstrapResumeIndex(batch.Checkpoints, batch.ResumeHash)
352			if err != nil && !batch.ResumeHash.IsZero() && len(batch.chain) > 0 {
353				// Temp ref doesn't match any planned checkpoint (e.g., the user
354				// changed --target-max-pack-bytes between runs). If the hash is
355				// in the commit chain, reuse it as the starting point and re-plan
356				// remaining checkpoints — preserving already-pushed data.
357				if chainIdx := chainPosition(batch.chain, batch.ResumeHash); chainIdx >= 0 {
358					remaining := batch.chain[chainIdx+1:]
359					if len(remaining) > 0 {
360						numBatches := estimateBatchCount(int64(len(remaining)), p.TargetMaxPack)
361						batch.Checkpoints = evenCheckpoints(remaining, numBatches)
362						p.log("bootstrap batch resuming from stale temp ref",
363							"branch", batch.Plan.TargetRef.String(),
364							"resume_hash", planner.ShortHash(batch.ResumeHash),
365							"remaining_commits", len(remaining),
366							"new_batches", len(batch.Checkpoints))
367						startIdx = 0
368						err = nil
369					}
370				}
371			}
372			if err != nil && !batch.ResumeHash.IsZero() {
373				// Temp ref hash not in the chain at all — truly stale. Delete and start fresh.
374				p.log("bootstrap batch clearing stale temp ref",
375					"branch", batch.Plan.TargetRef.String(),
376					"temp_ref", batch.TempRef.String(),
377					"stale_hash", planner.ShortHash(batch.ResumeHash))
378				delCmds := []gitproto.PushCommand{{Name: batch.TempRef, Old: batch.ResumeHash, Delete: true}}
379				if delErr := p.TargetPusher.PushCommands(ctx, delCmds); delErr != nil {
380					return result, fmt.Errorf("delete stale temp ref %s: %w (original: %w)", batch.TempRef, delErr, err)
381				}
382				current = plumbing.ZeroHash
383				startIdx = 0
384			}
385	
386			// Track every commit known to be in the target so the source
387			// can use them all as fetch haves. With topo ordering a merge's
388			// "delta" otherwise drags in the full ancestry of the non-first
389			// parent, even though we pushed those commits as their own
390			// checkpoints earlier in the chain (or in earlier runs).
391			//
392			// On resume, seed from the chain prefix at-or-before `current`:
393			// every prior topo iteration must have pushed those commits to
394			// advance the temp ref to its current position. Declaring just
395			// `current` is insufficient because in topo order the earlier
396			// chain entries aren't necessarily its ancestors — they can sit
397			// on side branches that only get merged later.
398			pushedCheckpoints := make([]plumbing.Hash, 0, len(batch.chain))
399			if !current.IsZero() && len(batch.chain) > 0 {
400				if idx := chainPosition(batch.chain, current); idx >= 0 {
401					pushedCheckpoints = append(pushedCheckpoints, batch.chain[:idx+1]...)
402				}
403			}
404	
405			// Manual index loop: subdivide may insert checkpoints at the current
406			// index, so we must not auto-increment after a retry.
407			idx := startIdx
408			for idx < len(batch.Checkpoints) {
409				checkpoint := batch.Checkpoints[idx]
410				if p.OnPhase != nil {
411					p.OnPhase(fmt.Sprintf("pack %d/%d", idx+1, len(batch.Checkpoints)))
412				}
413				p.log("bootstrap batch push checkpoint",
414					"branch", batch.Plan.TargetRef.String(),
415					"batch", idx+1,
416					"batch_total", len(batch.Checkpoints),
417					"from", planner.ShortHash(current),
418					"to", planner.ShortHash(checkpoint))

lines: +// replicateBootstrapRoute decides whether a replicate run should take the
+// bootstrap strategy instead of building replication plans, and with which
+// Besides the emptiness heuristic (replicateCanBootstrap), a leftover
+// refs/gitsync/bootstrap/* temp ref routes to bootstrap directly. The
+// namespace has exactly one writer — batched bootstrap, which deletes its
+// marker when the branch is finalized — so a surviving marker means a
+// bootstrap started and did not finish. Without this route, the marker is
+// just an undesired target ref that disqualifies the emptiness heuristic
+// under prune: the artifact of the one strategy that can resume is what
+// locked that strategy out, and the repo re-synced as a single unbatched
+// Marker routing deliberately ignores other stray target refs — an aborted
+// push or a branch deleted upstream mid-bootstrap must not re-wedge the
+// repo — but still requires every desired target ref to be absent, because
+// the bootstrap planner refuses targets whose desired refs exist. A marker
+// surviving next to its completed branch is stale; that state takes the
+// dropLiveBootstrapMarkerDeletes removes prune deletes for bootstrap temp
+// refs that still carry resume state — markers whose branch is desired but
+// absent on the target. That state is reachable only on a partially
+// bootstrapped target (some desired branch already complete, another still
+// mid-flight), which replicateBootstrapRoute cannot send to bootstrap; the
+// replicate run that handles it must not destroy the resume position, both
+// for a later bootstrap of the still-absent branch and as a fetch have that
+// shrinks this run's own pack. A marker whose branch exists or is no longer

567	// a benign concurrent-ref race, which lost a compare-and-swap to a competing
568	// sync of the same repo and self-heals on the next delivery. A race is tagged
569	// entire.sync.raced (queryable, mirroring the mirror.consume carve-out) but left
570	// un-errored, so it never shows as a failed mirror.sync span or counts toward an
571	// error-rate query on this span — matching the outcome metric's nak+term
572	// numerator, which also excludes raced. Exhaustion is a delivery-count concept
573	// the syncer can't see; the consumer still escalates a race that burns through
574	// redelivery to an error on the parent mirror.consume span (see
575	// shouldMarkSpanError). The race check uses the raw error, not the
576	// redacted/classified one, so redactAuth flattening the chain can't defeat it.
577	func markSyncSpanResult(span trace.Span, classified, raw error) {
578		if isConcurrentRefError(raw) {
579			span.SetAttributes(attribute.Bool("entire.sync.raced", true))

582		span.RecordError(classified)
583		span.SetStatus(otelcodes.Error, "sync from github")

608	// converged branch is the only reason this change exists, and it is invisible

Fixes [ENT-2054](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-2054/interrupted-batched-bootstrap-can-never-resume-the-resume-ref) — an interrupted batched bootstrap could never resume, because its own resume marker disqualified the bootstrap route. [ENT-1948](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1948/mirror-sync-permanently-fails-when-catch-up-pack-exceeds-10-gib) is one instance.

## The bug

Batched bootstrap writes `refs/gitsync/bootstrap/heads/<branch>` so an interrupted run can resume. Under `replicate --all-refs --prune` (the mirror-worker shape), that marker was just an undesired target ref of `RefKindOther`, so `replicateCanBootstrap` returned false and every subsequent sync routed to `replicate` — a single unbatched pack. The artifact of the one strategy that can resume is exactly what locked that strategy out, permanently.

## The fix

`replicateBootstrapRoute` now routes on the marker's presence, ahead of the emptiness heuristic. The namespace has exactly one writer — batched bootstrap, which deletes its marker on finalize or when stale — so a surviving marker is a positive signal: a bootstrap started and did not finish. The route requires every desired target ref to be absent (the bootstrap planner refuses targets whose desired refs exist) and deliberately ignores other stray target refs, so an aborted push or a branch deleted upstream mid-bootstrap cannot re-wedge the repo. The new reason `bootstrap-resume-marker` is threaded through dry-run too, so a plan against a stranded repo confirms the routing in one shot.

On the one partial shape the route cannot take (some desired branch complete, another mid-flight), replicate stays the executor; its prune plans now skip markers that still carry resume state (`dropLiveBootstrapMarkerDeletes`), so a best-effort run whose branch create is individually rejected cannot destroy the resume position. Markers whose branch exists or left the desired set stay prunable — replicate's prune is the only cleaner stale markers have.

## Deliberately not done

- **Deletes-before-updates in `replicate.Execute`** (floated in the ticket): the update-then-delete order is load-bearing for mirror-worker's default-branch rename recovery (`cmd/worker/defaultbranch.go:67`, recovery at `cmd/worker/syncer.go:464` in mirror-pipeline), which relies on the replacement branch existing before entiredb rejects the current-branch delete. Reordering would fire that rejection with the replacement absent and `SetDefaultBranch` would target a branch the mirror doesn't have. With routing fixed, marker cleanup no longer gates anything, so the reorder's benefit is cosmetic while its risk touches a recovery contract.
- **The `excludeRefPrefixes` stopgap in mirror-worker**: hiding `refs/gitsync/` from the sync scope would block stale-marker pruning forever, and it saves no deploy — stopgap and real fix both ship via a mirror-pipeline release.

## Caveats

- Small repos below the 1.5 GiB GitHub preflight threshold (with `TargetMaxPackBytes` unset) take the one-shot bootstrap path: a full re-transfer rather than a literal resume, with the marker pruned on the following run. Convergent — not a resume bug.
- The stranded repos (`gh/nicschick/vc3r`, `gh/nicschick/rci`) heal only once mirror-pipeline's git-sync pin is bumped past this and deployed. The companion observability change (logging `operation_mode`/`transfer_mode`/`relay_reason` from the worker) is independent and already on the same-named mirror-pipeline branch.

## Tests

- Routing table test (`TestReplicateBootstrapRoute`): marker+absent → bootstrap; marker+present → replicate; marker+stray ref → bootstrap; stray-only → replicate; empty → emptiness reason.
- `TestRun_IntegrationReplicateResumesInterruptedBatchedBootstrap`: interrupts a batched bootstrap mid-checkpoint under the exact mirror-worker shape, asserts the dry-run reports `bootstrap-resume-marker`, and asserts the retry's first temp-ref push resumes **from the marker hash** (not from zero), completes, and deletes the marker.
- Carve-out unit test (live marker delete dropped; stale/undesired markers and other deletes kept) and a `BootstrapTempRefTarget` round-trip test.

input.title: Bootstrap resume: partial-progress subset resume and a sync-mode route
input.description:
Fast-follow to ENT-2054 (git-sync PR [#116](https://github.com/entireio/git-sync/pull/116)). That PR makes an interrupted batched bootstrap resumable from its `refs/gitsync/bootstrap/*` marker under replicate, but two shapes remain outside the resume route — both surfaced and confirmed by the PR's code review.

## 1. Partial-progress resume (the sharpened remainder of the original wedge)

`replicateBootstrapRoute` requires **all** desired target refs to be absent, because `BuildBootstrapPlans` refuses targets whose desired refs exist. A multi-branch bootstrap interrupted **after any branch finalized** (trunk done, secondary branch mid-flight) therefore can never resume batching: the remaining branch goes as one unsubdividable replicate pack. The live marker is preserved and anchors the delta (PR #116's prune guard), so the pack shrinks relative to a fresh transfer — but if the residual delta exceeds the target's pack cap, the repo wedges exactly like ENT-2054.

Fix shape: subset bootstrap — when a live marker exists and *some* desired refs are absent, route only the absent subset through the bootstrap strategy (existing target refs already serve as haves via `completedRefs`). Needs decisions on mixed-run semantics: what the Result reports, that prune is skipped for the run, and that present branches stay stale until the next delivery (a dormant upstream means no next delivery — consider a follow-up kick).

## 2. Sync mode has no resume route at all

The routing lives in the replicate-only syncer method; `sync --all-refs --prune` against a marker-bearing target still disqualifies bootstrap via `planner.CanBootstrapRelay` (prune disables it outright, `relay.go`). Same wedge shape as the original ticket, different mode. PR #116 only fixed sync mode's destructive half (its prune no longer deletes live markers, via the shared `addPruneCandidates` exception). Wants the marker routing hoisted somewhere both modes share — likely the planner.

## Smaller items to sweep into whichever change touches the area

- **Stale marker under `Mappings` or branch-scoped prune has no cleaner**: `PruneTarget` only selects `RefKindOther` under AllRefs-without-Mappings, so an interrupted `--map` run leaves a marker that lingers forever (it no longer misroutes anything after PR #116's orphan fix — it just persists).
- **Dry-run doesn't disclose the one-shot path's marker deletes** (consistent with the batched temp-ref lifecycle, which dry-run also omits) — fold in if plan reporting is touched.
- **Reviewer suggestion**: the non-batchable-source integration test asserts the marker survives but not that it was sent as a fetch have; add the assertion if the test server grows negotiation capture.

{"body":"Read the full diff, ran the suite locally, probed a few shapes with throwaway tests.

The routing fix is right. Three things I verified hold up: `isLiveBootstrapMarker` at candidacy is the correct seam (`ActionDelete` is only emitted at `planner.go:167`/`:237`, both downstream, so nothing bypasses it); the removed `NoErrAlreadyUpToDate` branch really was dead (`gitproto` emits it only for `len(wants)==0`, and all three `Execute` callers gate on a non-empty desired set); and target refs are never prefix-narrowed, so the marker is always visible to the route. The integration test asserting `cmd.Old == marker.Hash()` pins the actual resume, not just the routing.

### 1. One-shot marker cleanup destroys resume state under `--best-effort`

`bootstrap.go:200-214`. The comment says *"every ref this bootstrap set out to create has landed"* — that's false when `OnRejection` is installed. `gitproto/push.go:453-470` swallows per-ref `ng` and returns `nil`, so `pushErr == nil` doesn't mean the create landed. `leftoverTempRefDeletes` then deletes the marker for a branch that doesn't exist. Probe (target rejects only the branch create, accepts the pack):

```
run result: relayMode="bootstrap" relayReason="bootstrap-resume-marker" err=<nil>
after run: branch present=false, marker present=false
```

Run reports success, branch absent, resume position gone. Reachable via CLI: `--all-refs` implies `BestEffort` for `bootstrap` (`cmd/git-sync/bootstrap.go:68`) and `sync` (`syncplan.go:121`), and `client.go:133` passes `Policy.BestEffort` through for any mode. Impact is bounded — one-shot is the small-repo path — but it's the exact hazard the replicate-side carve-out exists to prevent, left open on the path this PR adds.

Cheapest fix: drop the cleanup and let prune handle it. `isLiveBootstrapMarker` already classifies correctly (branch present → stale → pruned; absent → live → kept), which is the fallback the comment names anyway. Costs one extra run, can't be wrong.

**Pre-existing, related:** the batched cutover at `bootstrap.go:687-691` deletes the temp ref unconditionally with the create riding the same best-effort push at `:683`. Same probe fails identically on `origin/main`, so not a regression — but it belongs in ENT-2060 given this PR's subject.

### 2. Prune starvation if the bootstrap never completes

One run of delayed pruning is fine and documented. Not stated: if the bootstrap keeps failing, the marker survives, the route fires again, and prune is starved indefinitely — pre-PR those runs at least pruned. Worth a sentence in the routing comment.

### 3. PR body has drifted

It describes `dropLiveBootstrapMarkerDeletes` (gone as of c9423f7) and never mentions the source-side `refs/gitsync/*` discovery exclusion from 89b8c69 — a user-visible change beyond ENT-2054: such a source ref silently stops being mirrored, and a scaffolding-only source now hard-errors. The changelog is written from PR bodies, so that should land before merge.

### Minor

- Sync mode still labels a resume `empty-target-managed-refs` (`syncer.go:953`), so the new `relay_reason` signal doesn't reach `sync`. Already in ENT-2060.
- `desiredTargetRefsAbsent` runs twice on the bootstrap route.

input.command:
cat > /tmp/pr116-body.md <<'EOF'
Fixes [ENT-2054](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-2054/interrupted-batched-bootstrap-can-never-resume-the-resume-ref) — an interrupted batched bootstrap could never resume, because its own resume marker disqualified the bootstrap route. [ENT-1948](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1948/mirror-sync-permanently-fails-when-catch-up-pack-exceeds-10-gib) is one instance.

## The bug

Batched bootstrap writes `refs/gitsync/bootstrap/heads/<branch>` so an interrupted run can resume. Under `replicate --all-refs --prune` (the mirror-worker shape), that marker was just an undesired target ref of `RefKindOther`, so `replicateCanBootstrap` returned false and every subsequent sync routed to `replicate` — a single unbatched pack. The artifact of the one strategy that can resume is exactly what locked that strategy out, permanently.

## The fix

`replicateBootstrapRoute` routes on the marker's presence, ahead of the emptiness heuristic. The namespace has exactly one writer — batched bootstrap, which deletes its marker on finalize or when stale — so a surviving marker for a branch **in the desired set** is a positive signal: a bootstrap started and did not finish. The route requires every desired target ref to be absent (the bootstrap planner refuses targets whose desired refs exist) and deliberately ignores other stray target refs, so an aborted push or a branch deleted upstream mid-bootstrap cannot re-wedge the repo. It is gated on the source supporting batched bootstrap (protocol v2 + fetch filter); a non-batchable source stands down rather than trade a marker-anchored delta for a one-shot full pack. The reason `bootstrap-resume-marker` is threaded through dry-run, so a plan against a stranded repo confirms the routing in one shot.

**Marker lifecycle.** Prune is the marker's cleaner, and the exception that protects a live one is stated once, at prune candidacy (`addPruneCandidates`), so every plan builder is covered — including `sync --prune`, which previously would have deleted a resume position. A marker is live exactly while its branch is desired and absent; once the branch lands it is stale and prunes normally. Notably the bootstrap strategy does **not** delete the marker on the one-shot path: a nil push error doesn't prove the create landed (BestEffort swallows a per-ref `ng`), so deferring to prune costs one run and cannot be wrong. The one-shot path also passes target refs as fetch haves, so a small-repo resume transfers only the remainder.

## Behavior changes beyond the routing fix

- **`refs/gitsync/*` is no longer mirrored from a source.** Under `--all-refs`, a source ref in that namespace is now skipped by discovery. Such a ref is leftover scaffolding from that repo having been someone else's sync target, and mirroring it would collide with — and under replicate's overwrite semantics, clobber — this target's own resume marker. Consequence worth knowing: a source holding **only** that scaffolding now yields an empty desired set and errors (`no source refs matched` / `ErrNoRefsSelected`) where it previously converged. Deliberate; it clears once that source's own bootstrap resumes, which this PR is what makes possible.
- Target-side prune scope is unchanged — stale markers must stay reapable.

## Deliberately not done

- **Deletes-before-updates in `replicate.Execute`** (floated in the ticket): the update-then-delete order is load-bearing for mirror-worker's default-branch rename recovery (`cmd/worker/defaultbranch.go:67`), which relies on the replacement branch existing before entiredb rejects the current-branch delete. With routing fixed, marker cleanup no longer gates anything.
- **The `excludeRefPrefixes` stopgap in mirror-worker**: hiding `refs/gitsync/` from the sync scope would block stale-marker pruning forever, and saves no deploy.

## Known limitations — tracked in [ENT-2060](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-2060/bootstrap-resume-partial-progress-subset-resume-and-a-sync-mode-route)

- **Partial progress doesn't resume**: a multi-branch bootstrap interrupted after one branch finalized has a non-absent desired ref, so the remainder still goes as one replicate pack (marker-anchored, but unsubdividable).
- **Sync mode has no resume route** — only its destructive half is fixed here.
- Stale markers under `--map` or branch-scoped prune have no cleaner; the batched cutover deletes its temp ref on a best-effort create too (pre-existing, same hazard class as the one fixed here); dry-run doesn't disclose marker lifecycle.

## Rollout

`vc3r` / `rci` heal once mirror-pipeline's git-sync pin is bumped past this and deployed. The companion worker change — logging `operation_mode` / `transfer_mode` / `relay_reason`, whose absence is why ENT-2054 took a code read instead of a log query — is independent and on the same-named mirror-pipeline branch.

## Tests

- Routing table: marker+absent → bootstrap; marker+present branch → replicate; marker+stray ref → bootstrap; orphan marker → replicate; non-batchable source → replicate; no-prune resume labeling; empty target → emptiness reason.
- `TestRun_IntegrationReplicateResumesInterruptedBatchedBootstrap`: interrupts a batched bootstrap mid-checkpoint under the exact mirror-worker shape, asserts dry-run reports `bootstrap-resume-marker`, and asserts the retry's first temp-ref push resumes **from the marker hash** — not from zero.
- `TestRun_IntegrationResumeMarkerSurvivesBestEffortRejectedCreate`: a best-effort run whose branch create is rejected must leave the marker intact. Fails without the cleanup removal.
- `TestRun_IntegrationReplicateOrphanMarkerPrunedInOneRun`: pre-PR one-run parity for a marker whose branch was deleted upstream.
- Plus planner tests for the discovery exclusion and the prune guard (both builders), the non-batchable fallback, and one-shot resume (mid-chain and at-tip markers).

Full suite and golangci-lint green.

That PR makes an interrupted batched bootstrap resumable from its `refs/gitsync/bootstrap/*` marker under replicate, but two shapes remain outside the resume route — both surfaced and confirmed by the PR's code review.

## 1. Partial-progress resume (the sharpened remainder of the original wedge)

`replicateBootstrapRoute` requires **all** desired target refs to be absent, because `BuildBootstrapPlans` refuses targets whose desired refs exist. A multi-branch bootstrap interrupted **after any branch finalized** (trunk done, secondary branch mid-flight) therefore can never resume batching: the remaining branch goes as one unsubdividable replicate pack. The live marker is preserved and anchors the delta (PR #116's prune guard), so the pack shrinks relative to a fresh transfer — but if the residual delta exceeds the target's pack cap, the repo wedges exactly like ENT-2054.

Fix shape: subset bootstrap — when a live marker exists and *some* desired refs are absent, route only the absent subset through the bootstrap strategy (existing target refs already serve as haves via `completedRefs`). Needs decisions on mixed-run semantics: what the Result reports, that prune is skipped for the run, and that present branches stay stale until the next delivery (a dormant upstream means no next delivery — consider a follow-up kick).

## 2. Sync mode has no resume route at all

The routing lives in the replicate-only syncer method; `sync --all-refs --prune` against a marker-bearing target still disqualifies bootstrap via `planner.CanBootstrapRelay` (prune disables it outright, `relay.go`). Same wedge shape as the original ticket, different mode. PR #116 only fixed sync mode's destructive half (its prune no longer deletes live markers, via the shared `addPruneCandidates` exception). Wants the marker routing hoisted somewhere both modes share — likely the planner.

Related: sync mode also still labels a resume `empty-target-managed-refs` (`syncer.go:953`), so the new `relay_reason` signal never reaches `sync` — the routing hoist should fix the label with it.

## 3. Batched cutover deletes its temp ref on a create it cannot confirm

`bootstrap.go` cutover (~`:687`) deletes the temp ref unconditionally, while the branch create rides the preceding best-effort push. Under `BestEffort` the pusher swallows a per-ref `ng` and returns nil (`gitproto/push.go`, `OnRejection`), so a rejected create still reaches the delete — destroying the resume position for a branch that was never created.

**Pre-existing, not a regression:** the same probe fails identically on `origin/main`. PR #116 fixed exactly this hazard on the one-shot path (by dropping strategy-side cleanup and deferring to prune, which classifies a live marker correctly); the batched path wants the same treatment, or a rejection-aware signal plumbed into the strategy. Reachable from the CLI, where `--all-refs` implies best-effort for both `bootstrap` and `sync`.

* **Dry-run doesn't disclose marker lifecycle** (consistent with the batched temp-ref lifecycle, which dry-run also omits) — fold in if plan reporting is touched.

Heads-up on PR #116: Soph's human review found a real bug that all three automated passes missed — worth knowing about for calibration.

The bug: the one-shot marker cleanup I added (your earlier finding 5) is unsafe under --best-effort. gitproto/push.go:453-470 returns nil after handing a per-ref "ng" to OnRejection, so pushErr == nil does NOT mean the branch create landed — the cleanup then deleted the resume marker for a branch that doesn't exist. Run reports success, branch absent, resume position gone. Reachable from the CLI since --all-refs implies BestEffort. Exactly the hazard the replicate-side carve-out exists to prevent, left open on the path this PR added. Your pass 3 verdict 4 called the best-effort cleanup "correct" on the strength of my comment claiming every ref had landed; that claim was the false premise.

Fixed in 653e9c5 by dropping the cleanup entirely and letting prune own the marker (isLiveBootstrapMarker already classifies it correctly).

More important for your future passes: my first regression test PASSED WITHOUT THE FIX. A non-nil receivePackHook report short-circuits the integration test server before it applies any command, so a hook that denies indiscriminately makes marker-lifecycle assertions vacuous — the cleanup delete was reported ok and never executed, and the marker "survived" for the wrong reason. Fix is to pass ref-only pushes through (hasPack == false → return nil). I verified both directions by stashing only bootstrap.go: fails with "reference not found" on the un-fixed tree, passes with the fix. If you review marker-lifecycle tests in this repo again, that short-circuit is the thing to check first.

Also in from Soph and now tracked as ENT-2060 item 3: the batched cutover (bootstrap.go ~:687) has the same hazard pre-existing on origin/main — unconditional temp-ref delete after a best-effort create. Not a regression, recorded so nobody bisects it here.

PR body rewritten too (it still described dropLiveBootstrapMarkerDeletes and never mentioned the source-side refs/gitsync/ exclusion). No action needed from you unless you want to re-run over 653e9c5.

## 3. Batched cutover deletes its temp ref on a create it cannot confirm

`bootstrap.go` cutover (~`:687`) deletes the temp ref unconditionally, while the branch create rides the preceding best-effort push. Under `BestEffort` the pusher swallows a per-ref `ng` and returns nil (`gitproto/push.go`, `OnRejection`), so a rejected create still reaches the delete — destroying the resume position for a branch that was never created.

**Pre-existing, not a regression:** the same probe fails identically on `origin/main`. PR #116 fixed exactly this hazard on the one-shot path (by dropping strategy-side cleanup and deferring to prune, which classifies a live marker correctly); the batched path wants the same treatment, or a rejection-aware signal plumbed into the strategy. Reachable from the CLI, where `--all-refs` implies best-effort for both `bootstrap` and `sync`.

## 3. Batched cutover deletes its temp ref on a create it cannot confirm — highest priority item here

`bootstrap.go` cutover (~`:687`) deletes the temp ref unconditionally, while the branch create rides the preceding best-effort push. Under `BestEffort` the pusher swallows a per-ref `ng` and returns nil (`gitproto/push.go:453-470`, via `OnRejection`), so a rejected create still reaches the delete — destroying the resume position for a branch that was never created, and reporting the run as a success.

**Pre-existing, not a regression:** the reviewer's probe fails identically on `origin/main` and on PR #116's head. Recorded here so nobody bisects it to that PR.

**This is the higher-consequence half of the hazard PR #116 fixed.** Batched is the *large-repo* path — ENT-1948, the >10 GiB case the whole effort exists for — so a lost resume position here costs a full re-transfer of exactly the repos that can least afford one. `bootstrap --all-refs --target-max-pack-bytes=N` against a target that refuses the create loses an entire batched import, silently, reported as success.

Reachable from the CLI: `--all-refs` implies `BestEffort` for `bootstrap` (`cmd/git-sync/bootstrap.go:68`) and `sync` (`syncplan.go:121`), and `client.go:133` passes `Policy.BestEffort` through for any mode.

**PR #116's fix does not port.** That one dropped strategy-side cleanup and let prune own the marker; here that would leave a *permanent* marker, because `Bootstrap()` rejects `--prune` outright (`syncer.go:1305`) — no cleaner would ever exist on that path. The batched path needs the rejection actually threaded into the strategy instead. The syncer already records it (`s.rejections`, populated at `syncer.go:883/893`), so this is a `bootstrap.Params` field away rather than a redesign: delete the temp ref only when the branch create was not rejected.

## 1. Partial-progress resume (the sharpened remainder of the original wedge)

`replicateBootstrapRoute` requires **all** desired target refs to be absent, because `BuildBootstrapPlans` refuses targets whose desired refs exist. A multi-branch bootstrap interrupted **after any branch finalized** (trunk done, secondary branch mid-flight) therefore can never resume batching: the remaining branch goes as one unsubdividable replicate pack. The live marker is preserved and anchors the delta (PR #116's prune guard), so the pack shrinks relative to a fresh transfer — but if the residual delta exceeds the target's pack cap, the repo wedges exactly like <issue id="ca35a5b4-c595-4ffd-bf20-b7c1fd3dd331" href="https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-2054/interrupted-batched-bootstrap-can-never-resume-the-resume-ref">ENT-2054</issue>.

Fix shape: subset bootstrap — when a live marker exists and *some* desired refs are absent, route only the absent subset through the bootstrap strategy (existing target refs already serve as haves via `completedRefs`). Needs decisions on mixed-run semantics: what the Result reports, that prune is skipped for the run, and that present branches stay stale until the next delivery (a dormant upstream means no next delivery — consider a follow-up kick).

The routing lives in the replicate-only syncer method; `sync --all-refs --prune` against a marker-bearing target still disqualifies bootstrap via `planner.CanBootstrapRelay` (prune disables it outright, `relay.go`). content.text: An interrupted batched bootstrap leaves behind a resume marker that, being an unexpected extra ref on the target, disqualified the bootstrap strategy on every later sync — so the repo fell back to unbatched replicate forever and could never finish importing; the fix makes that marker *select* bootstrap instead, which resumes from the exact checkpoint it records.

message.content: what does the git-sync marker record?

attachment.turnReminder: Be concise: lead with the result, skip preamble and narration, keep only what the user needs.

content.text:
One ref per branch, and its whole payload is a single commit hash: `refs/gitsync/bootstrap/heads/<branch>` → the tip of the last checkpoint whose pack the target actually accepted. The name says which branch, the value says how far that branch got.

Nothing else is persisted — the commit chain, checkpoint placement, and batch sizing are all re-derived from the source on the next run. That's why resume tolerates a changed `--target-max-pack-bytes` between attempts: `BootstrapResumeIndex` looks for the marker's hash in the newly planned checkpoint list, and failing that `chainPosition` finds it in the first-parent/topo chain and re-plans the remainder from there. If the hash isn't in the chain at all (history rewritten upstream), the marker is deleted and the bootstrap starts fresh.

Two consequences worth knowing: progress is per-branch (a multi-branch bootstrap has one marker each, which is why partial progress is the ENT-2060 gap), and the hash doubles as a fetch *have* — the source only sends objects past that point, which is what makes a resumed run incremental rather than a re-download.

Brings ENT-2054's git-sync fix into the worker, plus the observability that should have made ENT-2054 a log query instead of a code read.

## What's here

**`532e872` — bump git-sync to `988d9f2`** (`v0.9.1-0.20260831085214-988d9f2730b5`, from [git-sync#116](https://github.com/entireio/git-sync/pull/116)). An interrupted batched bootstrap leaves a `refs/gitsync/bootstrap/*` resume marker on the target; under this worker's `replicate --all-refs --prune` shape that marker was just an undesired target ref, so it disqualified the bootstrap strategy on every later sync and the repo was routed to unbatched replicate forever. The artifact of the only strategy that could resume was what locked that strategy out. git-sync now routes on the marker and resumes from the checkpoint it records.

**`9b2fed3` — log the routing decision.** `operation_mode`, `transfer_mode`, `relay_reason` on "Sync complete". The worker recorded that a sync ran but never which strategy git-sync chose, which is precisely why ENT-2054 took a source read to diagnose rather than a query. A repo stuck on the wrong route is now one query away.

## Why this matters now

This is the half that heals the stranded repos. `gh/nicschick/vc3r` (`01KXK4WZWXD1PEP16K9V6CMFHA`, eu-central-1) has been wedged since 2026-07-15 behind a bootstrap marker with no `refs/heads/main`; `gh/nicschick/rci` (`01KXK4WZS7M270NSABM94DRF01`) is the same shape but latent — no sync jobs at all, so it takes the wedged path the moment a push arrives. Neither recovers until this deploys.

## Behavior change worth knowing

git-sync no longer mirrors `refs/gitsync/*` **from** a source under `--all-refs`. This worker is a caller with entiredb-kind sources, so it's the one that can see it: on a chained mirror (A → B → C) where B holds leftover bootstrap scaffolding, that namespace stops replicating to C. That's the intent — replicating it would collide with, and under replicate's overwrite semantics clobber, C's own resume marker. Consequence: a source holding *only* that scaffolding now errors (`no source refs matched`) where it previously converged. It clears once that source's own bootstrap finishes, which the same bump is what makes possible.

Target-side prune scope is unchanged, so stale markers stay reapable.

`go mod tidy`, `go build ./...`, and the full test suite pass on the new pin — no worker-side code changes were needed beyond the log line. Post-deploy, the signal to watch is `relay_reason=bootstrap-resume-marker` on the two repos above, followed by their first successful sync.

- **Partial-progress resume and a sync-mode route** — ENT-2060. A multi-branch bootstrap interrupted after one branch finalized still re-syncs the remainder as one replicate pack.
- **The batched cutover's best-effort temp-ref delete** — ENT-2060 item 3, pre-existing on git-sync main and independently reproduced (a completed 8-batch import reported as success with the marker destroyed). Soph is on it.
EOF
